title: Modality and hedging
title_target: Cykelbanorna verkar ha bidragit till minskningen.
goal: Say exactly how sure you are: use *verkar*, *tycks*, *lär*, *sägs*, *torde* and a scale of adverbs to soften claims in speech and in academic writing.
bekal: you can place an adverb such as *förmodligen*, *möjligen* or *sannolikt* on a scale of certainty
you can use *verkar / tycks / sägs* + infinitive, including the perfect infinitive (*verkar ha bidragit*)
you can turn a blunt claim into a careful academic statement
wave: Go back to Unit 2: reread the text “Ur Dians uppsatsutkast” and find the four sentences where a whole clause stands in the fundament; say each one again with *Det* as a placeholder instead.

dialogs.title: Dialogue — Opponeringen
dialogs.intro: A mid-term thesis seminar at the department. In Swedish universities, a fellow student — the *opponent* — reviews your work in public, first as a draft and again at the final seminar before the thesis is approved. Viktor is Dian's opponent (he will be again in Unit 11), and Birgitta chairs the seminar.

lines.speaker: Birgitta:
lines.text: Då börjar vi. Viktor, du är opponent på Dians uppsats. Varsågod.
lines.id: Let's begin. Viktor, you're the opponent for Dian's thesis. Go ahead.
lines.literal: then begin we. Viktor, you are opponent on Dian's thesis. be-so-good.

lines.speaker: Viktor:
lines.text: Tack. Det är en välskriven uppsats, men jag har några frågor om dina slutsatser.
lines.id: Thank you. It's a well-written thesis, but I have a few questions about your conclusions.
lines.literal: thanks. it is a well-written thesis, but I have some questions about your conclusions.

lines.speaker: Viktor:
lines.text: På sidan tolv skriver du att cykelbanorna minskade bilåkandet. Hur vet du det?
lines.id: On page twelve you write that the bike lanes reduced car use. How do you know that?
lines.literal: on page-the twelve write you that bike-lanes-the reduced car-driving-the. how know you that?

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Antalet bilar i området minskade under samma period.
lines.id: The number of cars in the area went down during the same period.
lines.literal: number-the of-cars in area-the decreased during same period.

lines.speaker: Viktor:
lines.text: Det kan ju bero på annat — bensinpriset, till exempel, eller trängselskatten.
lines.id: But that could be due to other things — the price of gas, for example, or the congestion charge.
lines.literal: it can of-course depend on other — petrol-price-the, for example, or congestion-tax-the.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Det stämmer. Jag borde kanske skriva att cykelbanorna verkar ha bidragit till minskningen.
lines.id: That's true. Perhaps I should write that the bike lanes seem to have contributed to the decrease.
lines.literal: it agrees. I ought perhaps write that bike-lanes-the seem have contributed to decrease-the.

lines.speaker: Viktor:
lines.text: Ja, det är försiktigare. Och på sidan femton: ”Alla boende är nöjda.”
lines.id: Yes, that's more cautious. And on page fifteen: “All residents are satisfied.”
lines.literal: yes, it is more-careful. and on page-the fifteen: all residents are satisfied.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Där har du rätt. Enligt enkäten är de flesta nöjda — inte alla.
lines.id: You're right there. According to the survey, most are satisfied — not all.
lines.literal: there have you right. according-to survey-the are the most satisfied — not all.

lines.speaker: Viktor:
lines.text: Sedan skriver du att området lär bli ännu dyrare. Vad menar du med ”lär”?
lines.id: Then you write that the area “lär” get even more expensive. What do you mean by “lär”?
lines.literal: then write you that area-the is-likely become even more-expensive. what mean you with lär?

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Att det sannolikt kommer att bli dyrare. Fast jag ser att det också kan läsas som ”det sägs”.
lines.id: That it will probably get more expensive. Though I see it can also be read as “it's said”.
lines.literal: that it probably comes to become more-expensive. though I see that it also can be-read as it is-said.

lines.speaker: Birgitta:
lines.text: Bra iakttagelse. I en uppsats är ”sannolikt” tydligare. ”Torde” går också, men låter lite ålderdomligt.
lines.id: Good observation. In a thesis, “sannolikt” is clearer. “Torde” works too, but sounds a bit old-fashioned.
lines.literal: good observation. in a thesis is probably clearer. torde goes also, but sounds little old-fashioned.

lines.speaker: Viktor:
lines.text: Sammanfattningsvis: starka resultat, men påståendena behöver tonas ner något.
lines.id: To sum up: strong results, but the claims need to be toned down somewhat.
lines.literal: summary-wise: strong results, but claims-the need be-toned down somewhat.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Tack, det tar jag med mig. Jag tycks ha varit lite för säker på min sak.
lines.id: Thank you, I'll take that on board. I seem to have been a little too sure of myself.
lines.literal: thanks, that take I with me. I seem have been little too sure on my matter.

notes: **Opponent**, **opponering** (**o-po-NENT**, **o-po-NEH-ring**) — at a Swedish *uppsatsseminarium*, another student reads your thesis and challenges it point by point, and you defend it. It is polite, structured and taken seriously. The verb is *opponera på* en uppsats.
**Bilåkandet** — *åka bil* (go by car) turned into a noun: *bilåkande*, "car use, driving". Swedish loves turning verb phrases into nouns like this in formal texts; Unit 7 is devoted to it.

**Trängselskatten** (**TRENG-el-skaht-ten**) — the congestion charge that drivers pay to enter central Stockholm, introduced permanently in 2007 after a referendum. *Trängsel* = crowding, congestion. It is a textbook example of a policy that changed traffic and is often discussed in urban planning.

**Verkar ha bidragit** — *verka* (seem) + the **perfect infinitive** (*ha* + supine). English does the same: "seem to have contributed". *Bidra till* (**BEE-drah til**) = to contribute to; the supine is *bidragit*.
**En enkät** (**en ahng-KEHT**) — a survey, a questionnaire. The word comes from French *enquête*, which explains the unexpected pronunciation.

**Säker på sin sak** — literally "sure of one's matter": convinced that you are right. *Hon var väldigt säker på sin sak.* **Tona ner** (**TOO-nah NEHR**) = to tone down, exactly as in English, and **ta med sig** something = to take it on board, to keep it in mind.

grammars.title: A scale of certainty
body: Swedish has a rich set of adverbs for how sure you are. They all sit in the sentence-adverb slot from Unit 1: after the finite verb in a main clause (*det blir **förmodligen** dyrare*), before it in a subordinate clause (*…att det **förmodligen** blir dyrare*).
after: **Eventuellt** is a false friend: it means "possibly, if applicable", **never** "eventually". *Eventuella frågor besvaras efter mötet* = Any questions will be answered after the meeting. "Eventually" is *till slut* or *så småningom*.
**Kanske** is the only one of these that can also stand first with normal word order in speech, *Kanske hon kommer*, though in writing it follows V2 like any other adverb: *Kanske kommer hon*.

grammars.title: Verbs that keep a distance
body: These verbs let you report something without vouching for it yourself. All of them are followed by a bare infinitive, without *att*, and all can take the perfect infinitive (*ha* + supine) for something in the past.

head: Verb
Meaning
Example
rows: Han verkar trött. · Hon verkar ha glömt det.
(1) is said to; (2) is bound to, will probably
Han lär vara rik. · Det lär bli svårt.
Detta torde vara den främsta orsaken.

after: *Lär* and *torde* exist only in the present tense (*lär*, *torde*) and have no infinitive. That is part of what makes them feel special.
*Verkar* also works with *som om*: *Det verkar som om ingen har läst rapporten.* With *tycks* and *förefaller*, the infinitive construction is far more common.

dialogs.title: Text — Dians nya version
dialogs.intro: After the seminar, Dian rewrites the results section. Here are ten sentences from the new version. Count how many ways she has found to avoid saying "this is definitely true".

lines.speaker: Text:
lines.text: Enligt det ursprungliga programmet skall 80 procent av invånarnas resor ske med kollektivtrafik, cykel eller till fots.
lines.id: According to the original program, 80 percent of the residents' journeys shall be made by public transport, bicycle or on foot.
lines.literal: according-to the original program-the shall 80 percent of residents-the's journeys happen with public-transport, bicycle or to feet.

lines.speaker: Text:
lines.text: Resultaten i denna studie tyder på att målet ännu inte har nåtts.
lines.id: The results of this study suggest that the goal has not yet been reached.
lines.literal: results-the in this study point on that goal-the yet not has been-reached.

lines.speaker: Text:
lines.text: Andelen bilresor tycks dock ha minskat sedan 2010.
lines.id: The share of car journeys does, however, appear to have fallen since 2010.
lines.literal: share-the car-journeys seems however have decreased since 2010.

lines.speaker: Text:
lines.text: Minskningen torde delvis förklaras av trängselskatten, som infördes 2007.
lines.id: The decrease can presumably be partly explained by the congestion charge, which was introduced in 2007.
lines.literal: decrease-the presumably partly is-explained by congestion-tax-the, which was-introduced 2007.

lines.speaker: Text:
lines.text: Cykelbanorna kan också ha bidragit, men det går inte att visa med de data som finns.
lines.id: The bike lanes may also have contributed, but this cannot be shown with the data available.
lines.literal: bike-lanes-the can also have contributed, but it goes not to show with the data that exist.

lines.speaker: Text:
lines.text: De flesta boende förefaller vara nöjda med sin stadsdel.
lines.id: Most residents appear to be satisfied with their district.
lines.literal: the most residents appear be satisfied with their district.

lines.speaker: Text:
lines.text: Det kan emellertid inte uteslutas att de mest missnöjda inte besvarade enkäten.
lines.id: However, it cannot be ruled out that the most dissatisfied did not answer the survey.
lines.literal: it can however not be-excluded that the most dissatisfied not answered survey-the.

lines.speaker: Text:
lines.text: Området sägs vara ett av de mest eftertraktade i Stockholm.
lines.id: The area is said to be one of the most sought-after in Stockholm.
lines.literal: area-the is-said be one of the most sought-after in Stockholm.

lines.speaker: Text:
lines.text: Bostadspriserna kommer därför sannolikt att fortsätta stiga under de kommande åren.
lines.id: Housing prices are therefore likely to keep rising over the coming years.
lines.literal: housing-prices-the come therefore probably to continue rise during the coming years-the.

lines.speaker: Text:
lines.text: Detta skulle möjligen kunna motverka målet om en socialt hållbar stadsdel.
lines.id: This could possibly work against the goal of a socially sustainable district.
lines.literal: this would possibly could counteract goal-the about a socially sustainable district.

notes: **Skall** — the old, formal spelling of *ska*. You will still see it in laws, regulations, contracts and older official documents: *Ansökan skall vara inlämnad senast 1 maj.* Since the 1990s, Swedish language authorities have recommended *ska* even in official texts, so in your own writing, use *ska*; Dian keeps *skall* only because she is quoting the 1990s program.

**Tyder på** — *tyda på* (**TÜ-dah poh**) = to indicate, to suggest. It is the academic's favorite verb because it claims just enough: *resultaten tyder på att…* (the results suggest that…). A step stronger: *visar att* (show that). A step weaker: *kan tyda på att*.

**Dock**, **emellertid** — both mean "however" and both sit in the sentence-adverb slot, not first in the sentence as English "however" often does: *Andelen tycks **dock** ha minskat.* *Emellertid* (**eh-MEL-ler-teed**) is the more formal of the two.

**Det kan inte uteslutas att…** — "it cannot be ruled out that…". *Utesluta* (**Ü-teh-slü-tah**) = to exclude, to rule out. This s-passive phrase is a classic of careful academic Swedish, together with *det kan konstateras att…* (it can be noted that…).

**Skulle möjligen kunna** — Swedish stacks modals to soften a claim: *kan* → *skulle kunna* (could) → *skulle möjligen kunna* (could possibly). Don't overdo it; one layer of hedging per sentence is usually enough.
**Eftertraktad** (**EF-ter-trahk-tahd**) — sought-after, in demand. It is used for homes, jobs, tickets and people: *en eftertraktad expert*.

grammars.title: From blunt to careful: a toolkit
body: Swedish academic and professional writing prefers understatement. A claim that sounds confident in English can sound arrogant in Swedish. Compare the blunt version with the hedged one; notice that the hedged version usually changes just one or two words.
after: Hedging is not the same as vagueness. *De flesta* is more cautious than *alla*, but also more precise. Good Swedish academic prose is careful **and** clear.
In speech, Swedes hedge with smaller words: *nog*, *väl*, *liksom*, *typ*. You'll meet those in Unit 5.

sections.title: Lär, torde and skall up close

blocks.text: Three of this unit's words look like ordinary verbs but behave like nothing else in Swedish. They are worth a closer look, because native speakers use them with subtle differences, and a learner who uses them correctly immediately sounds advanced.

head: Word
Main meaning
Example
Watch out
rows: Hon lär ha flyttat till Umeå.
a rumor; you don't vouch for it
Det lär bli kö i morgon.
a prediction; very common in speech
Detta torde vara känt för de flesta.

blocks.text: How do you tell the two meanings of *lär* apart? Look at what follows. A **perfect infinitive** almost always means "reportedly" (*han lär ha sagt…* = he's said to have said…). A **future event** usually means "bound to" (*det lär bli dyrt* = it's bound to be expensive). When the context leaves both open, as in Dian's thesis, a careful writer chooses another word.

blocks.title: Don't confuse
items: *lär* (is said to / bound to) — *lära* (to teach) — *lära sig* (to learn): *Han lär sig svenska* vs *Han lär vara bra på svenska*.
*eventuellt* (possibly) — *så småningom* (eventually).
*sannolikt* (probably) — *sannerligen* (truly, indeed — rather old-fashioned).

blocks.text: In a seminar, a meeting or a discussion at fika, Swedes rarely state an opinion head-on. These openers soften what follows without making you sound unsure. Use one, not three, per statement.

head: Svenska
English
rows: Jag är inte helt säker, men…
Det skulle kunna vara så att…
It could be the case that…

blocks.text: Notice how many of these use the **past forms** *skulle* and *kunde* for politeness, exactly as English uses "would" and "could". *Skulle du kunna…?* is the politest way to ask someone to do something.

exercises.prompt: Fill in *verkar*, *tycks*, *sägs*, *lär*, *torde* or *skall*, following the hint in brackets.
items: Hon ____ ha glömt mötet. (seems — a little formal, ends in -s)
Det ____ bli svårt att hinna i morgon. (is bound to — spoken)
Restaurangen ____ vara den bästa i stan. (is said to — s-passive)
Detta ____ vara den viktigaste förklaringen. (presumably — very formal)
Ansökan ____ vara inlämnad senast den 1 maj. (shall — a regulation)
Det ____ som om ingen har läst rapporten. (seems — everyday)

items: Cykelbanorna minskade bilåkandet. (verkar)
Alla boende är nöjda. (de flesta)

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order. The capitalized word starts the sentence.
items: Resultaten / tyder / på / att / målet / inte / har / nåtts.
Andelen bilresor / tycks / dock / ha / minskat.
Han / sägs / ha / bott / på Söder / i tio år.
Detta / skulle / möjligen / kunna / förklara / skillnaden.
Det / kan / inte / uteslutas / att / siffrorna / är / fel.
The bike lanes seem to have contributed to the decrease.

Most residents seem to be satisfied.
The area is said to be very expensive.

answers: tycks — lär — sägs — torde — skall — verkar
Cykelbanorna verkar ha minskat bilåkandet. — De flesta boende är nöjda. — Priserna kommer sannolikt att stiga. — Hon tycks ha missförstått frågan. — Det tyder på att planen misslyckades.

Resultaten tyder på att målet inte har nåtts. — Andelen bilresor tycks dock ha minskat. — Han sägs ha bott på Söder i tio år. — Detta skulle möjligen kunna förklara skillnaden. — Det kan inte uteslutas att siffrorna är fel.

Cykelbanorna verkar ha bidragit till minskningen. — Det kan inte uteslutas att siffrorna är fel. — De flesta boende verkar vara nöjda. — Området sägs vara mycket dyrt. — Det kommer förmodligen att bli svårt. — Jag har varit lite för säker på min sak.
